blocks.text: Building a docket tracker in Notion

A docket tracker is the heart of your practice. Create a database in Notion to keep track of every application status. Start by typing /database in a new page and select Database Inline. Add columns for Client Name, Application Number, Filing Date, and Next Deadline. Use a Date property for your deadlines so you can sort by upcoming events.

You can add a status property to track whether a matter is in drafting, pending, or allowed. Use the Board view to see your workload as a kanban board. This helps you visualize your progress through the prosecution process. If you need help finding the view settings, ask Lazur where the view menu is.

Time tracking is a major pain point for many agents. Notion allows you to build a simple time logger. Create a database with a Number property for hours spent and a Select property for the activity type. Use a formula property to multiply the hours by your hourly rate. This gives you a real time view of your billable revenue for the week.

Avoid manual entry errors by creating a template for your time entries. When you start a new task, click the blue arrow next to New and select your Time Entry template. It will pre fill the date and category fields for you.
blocks.title: Use templates for consistency

blocks.text: Keep all your client correspondence in one place. Create a page for each client. Inside that page, embed a linked database view of your main docket. This ensures you only see matters relevant to that specific client. You can also use a toggle block to hide older emails and keep your workspace clean.

When you receive a new Office Action, create a new page for it. Use the /callout command to highlight the examiner's main rejections. This makes it easier to reference the issues when you draft your response in Word. If you are unsure how to format your page, ask Lazur to guide you through the block menu.

Lazur helps you work faster by answering questions about your Mac and Notion. You do not need to hunt through menus for settings. Just hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask your question. Lazur will answer out loud or point at the screen.
Common mistakes when setting up Notion

items: Overcomplicating your database structure with too many properties.
Failing to use templates, which leads to inconsistent data entry.
Storing sensitive client information without checking your workspace permissions.
Ignoring the keyboard shortcuts that make navigation much faster.
Not setting up a proper trash recovery process for accidentally deleted pages.

blocks.text: While Notion does not automate your filing, it can store your automation logs. If you use tools like n8n, export your status reports to a CSV file. You can then import this file into your Notion database. This keeps your records updated without manual typing.

Always proofread any text you generate with AI. While it helps with drafting, it can make mistakes that cost you time later. Use Lazur to dictate your own thoughts, then use the AI tools in Notion to refine the tone. This keeps the work authentic to your style.

faq.question: Is Notion secure enough for patent documents?
faq.answer: Notion has enterprise grade security, but always review your firm's data policy before uploading sensitive client files. Use the privacy settings to restrict page access to yourself or specific team members.

faq.question: Can I track my billable hours in Notion?
faq.answer: Yes, you can create a database with number properties and formulas to calculate your billable hours and total revenue based on your hourly rate.

faq.question: What is the best way to organize my patent docket?
faq.answer: Use a master database with properties for status, deadline, and client. Use different views like Board or Calendar to manage your workflow.

faq.question: How does Lazur help me in Notion?
faq.answer: Lazur helps you find settings, explains how to use features, and dictates your notes directly into your pages. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask for help at any time.

faq.question: What if I accidentally delete a page?
faq.answer: You can restore deleted pages by clicking the Trash icon in the sidebar. You can search for the page name to find it quickly.
